opening.argument: The segment presents the Walmart gift-card message as a warning, not an offer from the presenter or broadcaster. A news presenter displays the message and its claim link, while the broadcast identifies it as a text-message scam. The reporting explains why viewers should not click the link and advises anyone who receives an unsolicited text claiming they have won a gift card to delete it. An interview subject identified as being from the Better Business Bureau appears as part of that reporting. The link and promised card are therefore the subject of the consumer warning, not an invitation by the segment to claim a reward.

citations.quote: TINA JENSON HAS MORE ON WHY YOU DON'T WANT TO CLICK ON THE LINK.
SO IF YOU GET A UNSOLICITED TEXT MESSAGE THAT YOU'VE WON A GIFT CARD, THE BEST THING YOU CAN DO IS HIT DELETE.
